authorization: The user explicitly requested the approved server-database recommendation plan be implemented and put online.
objective: Search plugin purpose and keywords in a private server-side SQLite FTS5 index, enrich selected rows from a locally verified versioned Store Catalog, and periodically synchronize the index from the newest valid local Pages release without GitHub requests during user searches.

implementation.index: Use SQLite FTS5 with the server Python standard library through a persistent JSON-lines worker; add no npm SQLite dependency. Index only package names, display names, aliases, short purpose text, search terms, categories, status, and pinned Commit.
implementation.enrichment: After SQL retrieval, enrich only the bounded candidate set from the in-memory Catalog snapshot verified against its versioned release manifest. Do not request GitHub on recommendation requests.
implementation.sourceSelection: Inspect local /opt/dsh-store/current and /opt/dsh-store-cn/current releases, validate both manifests and their build-manifest.json and registry/catalog.json size/SHA-256 entries, and select the newest valid generatedAt. Keep the last valid database if a source fails validation.
implementation.synchronization: Build a replacement index in one SQLite transaction at process start and poll local release manifests every five minutes. Refresh only when the verified Catalog SHA changes.
implementation.storage: Use /var/lib/dsh-model-service/plugin-catalog.sqlite3 in production with owner-only database and directory permissions. Do not store model credentials, plugin source code, or full user requests.
implementation.recommendationBoundary: SQLite returns a bounded shortlist; the shared semantic matcher still filters to approved entries pinned to a full Commit; the configured LLM may explain only those candidates.

deterministicGates: Disposable SQLite fixtures prove FTS retrieval, Chinese bigram search, approved/full-Commit filtering, transactional replacement, and status metadata.
A release fixture with mismatched Catalog hash or build/source Commit is rejected and leaves the last valid index usable.
The exact image-reading request returns only relevant approved fixed-Commit candidates through the SQLite shortlist.
The recommendation API and public catalog-status endpoint report the SQLite index; API-key and encrypted model settings are unchanged.
Recommendation requests use only SQLite and the verified local release snapshot; no GitHub request is made per user query.
npm run check and both static marketplace builds pass; changes are published through the existing CI-checked PR.

Each server deployment verifies current release and service-unit precondition hashes, writes a versioned service release, keeps the previous release for rollback, restarts the service, and reads back health, SQLite metadata, and a relevant sample query.
rollback: Keep the previous service release and atomically restore the current symlink if restart or health/readback fails. SQLite source replacement is transactional; on application rollback, retain the database file and model configuration unchanged.
